< |im_END| 2025-10-13T02:04:16.282Z|>The current solution is a well-tuned 3-member ensemble (LightGBM ordinal-encoded, CatBoost native categoricals, entity-embedding MLP) with holdout-tuned blend weights and decision threshold, achieving 0.7635 held-out accuracy on 8117 training rows. Improvement should come from enriching the feature representation that such a tree-heavy ensemble is weak at capturing, since the categorical interactions driving coupon acceptance (coupon type × time-of-day × distance × customer habit affinity) are only partially encoded by the single 'coupon_time' interaction.

CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: [Category: Data Augmentation / Feature Engineering]
- What: Replace the current single engineered interaction 'coupon_time' with a systematic set of task-specific interaction features: (a) coupon × distance_level, (b) coupon × time_hour, (c) coupon × expiration, (d) coupon × coupon_affinity binned, (e) customer-habit aggregate (mean of the five FREQ_COLS) and its deviation from the coupon_affinity value (habit-mismatch signal), (f) occupation × income composite ordinal, and (g) an "acceptance-prevalence" style count-encoding of the highest-cardinality categoricals (occupation, coupon×time, age×income) fit ONLY on training rows and smoothed with add-k. All new features are computed inside FeatureBuilder.fit/transform so they persist in the artifact and are applied identically in the fresh predict process.
- Why: Coupon acceptance is strongly conditional on the match between the offered coupon type and the customer's existing venue habits, plus whether the trip distance/time makes the offer reachable. Tree models split axis-aligned on ordinal codes and cannot easily recover these conjunctions (e.g., 'Bar' coupon accepted only when Bar-habit>=2 and time=6PM/10PM and distance<=15min). Providing these conjunctions explicitly and habit-mismatch as a continuous scalar gives the ensemble the interaction structure it currently has to approximate through depth, which is exactly where it underfits on 8k rows.

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: Under-powered feature interactions, not model capacity. The ensemble already regularizes well (holdout weights are stable and the MLP isn't overfitting), but the only explicit interaction is coupon_time; conjunction effects like coupon×habit-affinity and coupon×distance drive the label and are being learned implicitly by trees from ordinal codes, which is notoriously sample-inefficient for 3-way interactions on a few thousand rows.
- Evidence: The dataset has only 21 columns with 5 low-cardinality coupon types and 5 ordinal habit columns; nearly all predictive signal in this problem (literature-standard ~76-79% accuracy) comes from a handful of conditional rules involving coupon type, time, distance thresholds, and prior habit levels. The current 0.7635 is at the low end of that range, and the holdout-tuned ensemble barely outperforms a single CatBoost, indicating the marginal value is limited by representation, not by ensembling.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: Explicit conjunction features give axis-aligned tree learners a single split that directly encodes a multi-way rule (e.g., coupon_affinity==0 & distance_level==3 → low acceptance), reducing the depth and sample count needed to learn it; the habit-mismatch scalar supplies a smooth, monotone signal the MLP can exploit; smoothed training-only count encodings of high-cardinality combos provide a target-correlated but leakage-safe density cue. Because these are all deterministic functions of inputs (plus training-fitted smoothed counts), they are computed once and shared across all three ensemble members, improving each simultaneously with no extra inference cost.
- Expected improvement: +0.5 to +1.2 percentage points held-out accuracy (0.769-0.775), with the largest gain coming from CatBoost and MLP since they benefit most from explicit interaction structure and smooth signals respectively. Synergy: better features reduce variance across members, which typically stabilizes the holdout weight search as well.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: 42
- Data split: identical 85/15 stratified holdout on training rows for weight/threshold tuning, and the same 88/12 split for the final MLP early stopping
- Model architectures: LGBM (400 trees, lr 0.05, 31 leaves), CatBoost (400 iters, depth 6, native cats), EntityEmbeddingMLP (256-128-64, dropout 0.20)
- Weight/threshold tuning procedure: same grid search over simplex weights (step 10) and thresholds 0.30-0.70
- Label mapping logic and output format (row_id, prediction with original labels)
- All leakage-safety guarantees: everything fit on training rows only; predict loads artifact and never refits
